Let $T=[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ What is the image of the square $R$ (shown above) above under the action of $T?$

Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/6231eb09a75376d694a6f47c47cf5a26aab4a32c28b2799f7e1f0825a7017f88.png) be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}.$ What is the image of the square $R$ (shown above) under the action of $\mathbf{T}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Looking at the matrix $T,$ we can see that $\mathbf{T}$ represents a vertical shear of shear factor $-1.$ Therefore, the image of the square $R$ under $\mathbf{T}$ is as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062085/assets/2d3d15c4d6b6f9e08c6fbcc35236b50dcd6cf4d09e9204e0aa255706461c3dd8.png)

**Alternative method:**

We can check that the vertices of $R$ are mapped to the vertices of the parallelogram shown above as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
What linear transformation $T$ is represented by the following matrix
$[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the images of the standard basis vectors $i$ and $j$ under the action of  $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=2i \\ T(j) & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix represents a stretch of scale factor $2$ in the $x$-direction.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A stretch of scale factor $2$ in the $x$-direction
